subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox prune does not clean up workspace directory

question: Should this focused prune-workspace leak be fixed now with a narrow backend-aware cleanup, or should it wait for the broader managed sandbox lifecycle work?
rationale: Both approaches can solve the user-visible stale workspace leak, but recursive workspace deletion is destructive state cleanup and the broader lifecycle branch is already changing the same ownership boundary.

options.title: Land narrow prune cleanup
options.body: Fix this bug directly by deleting only eligible non-shared sandbox-owned workspaces after confirmed runtime removal, with focused regression coverage for scope and active-workspace safety.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle branch
options.body: Keep this issue open as acceptance criteria for the managed lifecycle work and close it only after that branch lands with exact proof of runtime plus workspace cleanup.

options.title: Pause new cleanup work
options.body: Hold new repair attempts until maintainers resolve the broader lifecycle direction and the closed unsafe cleanup attempts are no longer informative blockers.

recommendation.title: Land narrow prune cleanup
recommendation.body: Fix this bug directly by deleting only eligible non-shared sandbox-owned workspaces after confirmed runtime removal, with focused regression coverage for scope and active-workspace safety.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest sandbox lifecycle history and owns the overlapping managed lifecycle direction.
